clue.text: Father-he's not quite disposed to press his suit

parts.note: pop is an informal name for one's father

indicators.note: disposed in the sense of arranged or set out anew, so the letters of these words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A dad who is not quite ready to go on with a court case or a courtship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disposed' rearranges HESNOTQUITE (from 'he's not quite') into THEQUESTION, which follows POP for Father.
explanation.definitionFit: To press one's suit is to woo, and proposing marriage is the culmination of that wooing.

clue.text: East German in spotless carriage

indicators.note: in places the German word inside the word for spotless

parts.note: spotless means clean or pure
Ost is the German word for east

explanation.surface: An East German sitting in an immaculate horse-drawn carriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' is not a person but the German word for east, OST, set inside PURE.
explanation.definitionFit: Carriage here means bearing or the way one holds the body, a synonym.

clue.text: Informed that one was included in the photo-call

definitions.text: one was included in the photo-call

explanation.surface: Someone told they had been included in the shot at a photo session.
explanation.definitionFit: To be told the facts is to be brought up to date; literally, someone placed in a photograph has been included in its frame.

clue.text: Criminal spoils gold in the Upper Chamber

indicators.note: in puts the gold symbol within the abbreviation for the chamber

parts.note: the House of Lords is the UK Parliament's upper chamber, abbreviated HL
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: Ill-gotten gold found stashed in the House of Lords.
explanation.walkthrough: HL is the abbreviation for the House of Lords, Britain's upper chamber of Parliament.
explanation.definitionFit: A thief's take or loot is commonly called a haul, a synonym.

clue.text: Friend who trembles with terror

explanation.surface: A companion shaking with fear.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of the Religious Society of Friends are known by that nickname; literally, one who shakes with fear.

clue.text: Inspector upset woodcutter and collier

indicators.note: upset in a down clue means turned upside down, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: an axe is a tool for cutting wood
a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: An official upsets a lumberjack and a coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woodcutter' is the tool, not the person: AXE, turned up by 'upset' to give EXA, before MINER.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector checks and scrutinises things, as an examiner of documents or candidates does.

clue.text: The other man or woman from the Liberal Democrats

explanation.surface: The other man or woman in a love triangle comes from a centrist political party.
explanation.walkthrough: The Liberal Democrats are traditionally Britain's third-largest political party after Labour and the Conservatives.
explanation.definitionFit: A person outside the two main parties to a matter is an outsider in a dispute; the Lib Dems have long been Britain's third force.

clue.text: By some method palindromes can thus be read

explanation.surface: A remark on how word puzzles that read the same both ways may be tackled.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means by any means at all; literally, a palindrome reads identically forwards or backwards.

clue.text: Includes a divine child

parts.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, stands for a clergyman or divine
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A family takes in a holy infant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' is a noun here, a clergyman, abbreviated DD for Doctor of Divinity.
explanation.definitionFit: To include extra items is to put them in addition, a phrasal synonym.

clue.text: Bring back a necessity like some citrus fruit

indicators.note: bring back asks for the whole run of pieces to be read from right to left

parts.note: a must is something essential
as means like, in the manner of

explanation.surface: A demand to bring back an essential item, such as citrus fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring back' turns the whole run A MUST AS around.
explanation.definitionFit: A satsuma is a type of mandarin orange, an example of citrus fruit.

clue.text: Aromatic flavouring found recurrently in a grain

indicators.note: recurrently read as running back again, so the little word goes backwards

parts.note: a grain of a cereal is its seed

explanation.surface: A spice discovered time and again inside a grain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recurrently' turns IN into NI, which sits between A and SEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Anise seed is used to give a liquorice taste to food and drink, a spice.

clue.text: Vessels held by taciturn sailors

indicators.note: held by signals letters kept within the run of words that follow

explanation.surface: Containers carried by sailors who say little.
explanation.walkthrough: 'held by' points to the letters running across 'taciturn sailors'.
explanation.definitionFit: Urns are pots or containers, a kind of vessel.

clue.text: Where landlords serve ale in jug

explanation.surface: A description of pub landlords pouring beer into a pitcher.
explanation.definitionFit: Publicans stand behind the counter to serve; jug is slang for jail, where inmates are locked up.

clue.text: Bucks take to wine and hunting

parts.note: bucks and bloods are old words for dashing young men
port is a fortified wine

explanation.surface: Young men take to drink and the chase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bucks' means dandies, not deer, despite the hunting surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Fox hunting and similar field pursuits that kill animals are classed as blood sports, an example.

clue.text: When immersed in a river Henry has to breathe out

indicators.note: immersed in places the name within the river, as a swimmer would be

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon, England
Hal is a pet form of Henry, as in Prince Hal

explanation.surface: Henry, dunked in a river, needs to let out his breath.
explanation.walkthrough: The EXE is a river in south-west England; HAL, for Henry, goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhale is to expel air from the lungs, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Receive credit for negotiating a long tea-break

indicators.note: negotiating in the sense of working through or manoeuvring, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Being rewarded for bargaining a lengthy break for tea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'negotiating' rearranges ALONGTEA; 'break' adds to the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Credit means borrowed money, so obtaining it is securing an advance from a lender.

clue.text: One reeks terribly of paraffin

indicators.note: terribly signals the letters of the preceding words are mangled

explanation.surface: Someone who smells strongly of lamp oil.
explanation.definitionFit: Paraffin is the British name for lamp oil, which Americans call by this name.

clue.text: Piped down when Sidney was about to call

indicators.note: about means around, so the short name wraps the word for call

parts.note: Sid is short for Sidney
to phone is to call

explanation.surface: Sidney was told to pipe down as he was about to make a call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Piped down' looks like an order to be quiet, but it means drawn off through a pipe.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid drawn down a tube from a higher container has been drained through a pipe.

clue.text: Small Irish lake and marsh

parts.note: lough is the Irish word for a lake

explanation.surface: A little Irish lake next to boggy ground.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or bog, a synonym.

clue.text: Singular characteristic displayed by a channel

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular
a trait is a distinguishing characteristic

explanation.surface: A unique feature shown by a waterway.
explanation.definitionFit: A strait is a narrow stretch of sea between two land masses, a synonym.

clue.text: Set out to become a spectacular success

explanation.surface: A venture leaves and does brilliantly.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking off is departing, as a plane leaves the ground; a career that soars suddenly has done so too.

clue.text: Pulp that is produced from iron

parts.note: mash is pulped matter
ie is the abbreviation of id est, that is

explanation.surface: Pulp produced from metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'iron' is a golf club, not the metal; the mashie is an old club.
explanation.definitionFit: A mashie is an old name for the golf club now called the five-iron.

clue.text: Every now and then casino is involved in coal production

definitions.note: an adverb phrase standing for an adjective meaning intermittent, as in an occasional visitor

indicators.note: production signals the letters are worked into a new form

explanation.surface: From time to time a casino becomes part of coal mining.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening at irregular intervals is the sense of intermittent, a near synonym.

clue.text: Overcharge for a castle

explanation.surface: Charging too much for a fortress.
explanation.definitionFit: To rook is to swindle a customer; the chess piece shaped like a tower is also called a castle.

clue.text: Move up 17 yards

annotationWithheld.why: Move up 17 yards: 'Move up' defines LIFT but '17 yards' fits no parse with 17-across SIPHONED or 17-down SLOUGH; likely OCR or cross-reference garble, no source found

clue.text: Sugar and crisp lettuce put into a paste

indicators.note: put into places the lettuce within the word for paste

parts.note: glue is an adhesive paste
cos is a crisp variety of lettuce

explanation.surface: Sugar and crunchy lettuce mixed into a paste.
explanation.walkthrough: COS, a crisp long-leaved lettuce, goes inside GLUE.
explanation.definitionFit: Glucose is a simple sugar, an example.

clue.text: Weary cry from Egyptian imprisoned in tall house

indicators.note: imprisoned in places the letter within the word for tall

parts.note: tall means high
E is an abbreviation for Egyptian, as in E pounds

explanation.surface: An Egyptian sighs while locked inside a tall building.
explanation.definitionFit: Heigh-ho is an exclamation of boredom or resignation, a tired sigh.

clue.text: Buy the product which is superior-or worst!

definitions.text: Buy the product which is superior

explanation.surface: Advice to purchase the better item, or else the worst one.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally, acquire the finer item; to worst someone is to defeat them, which is to overcome them.
